summary: A comprehensive plan to add 1-on-1 and group voice/video calls to TruckConnect using LiveKit as the WebRTC SFU infrastructure, supporting all devices (smartphone, tablet, desktop).

alternatives_considered.name: Pure WebRTC + Ably Signaling
cons: Peer-to-peer only (no SFU = bad for 3+ users)
Complex NAT traversal logic to build manually
No mesh = high CPU on mobile for group calls

alternatives_considered.name: Twilio Video
cons: Overkill pricing for a fleet app

why_livekit: 100% open source (Apache 2.0) – self-host on existing Docker infra
SFU architecture – scales from 1:1 to group calls without P2P mesh overhead
First-class React SDK (@livekit/components-react) – fits Next.js perfectly
Works natively on iOS Safari, Android Chrome, iPad, Desktop browsers
Built-in TURN server via LiveKit Egress/Ingress + relay support
Supports audio-only mode (voice calls) and video calls with the same SDK
Room-based model maps perfectly to trucker conversations
LiveKit Cloud available if self-hosting becomes a burden
Active ecosystem: recording, transcription, SIP integration for future

architecture.overview: LiveKit Server runs as a sidecar Docker container alongside the Next.js app and PostgreSQL. Ably continues to handle all existing real-time events. LiveKit handles only call signaling and media relay. The Next.js backend issues LiveKit access tokens via a new /api/calls/* route group.

client_connects_to: LiveKit Server (WebRTC media + signaling via WSS)
Next.js API (REST: create room, get token, end call)
nextjs_server_connects_to: LiveKit Server REST API (room management, token generation)
Ably (publish call_incoming / call_ended events to callee)
livekit_server_connects_to: TURN (built-in LiveKit relay OR Cloudflare TURN free tier)

call_flow.step_1_caller_initiates: Caller hits POST /api/calls/initiate with { calleeId, type: 'voice'|'video' }
call_flow.step_2_server_creates_room: Server calls LiveKit API: CreateRoom({ name: 'call-{uuid}', emptyTimeout: 30 })
call_flow.step_3_server_issues_tokens: Server generates two JWT tokens (caller + callee) via livekit-server-sdk
call_flow.step_4_notify_callee: Server calls ablyPublish('user:{calleeId}', 'call_incoming', { roomName, token, callerInfo, type })
call_flow.step_5_callee_ui: Callee sees incoming call modal (accept / decline)
call_flow.step_6_accept: Both clients join the LiveKit room using their tokens
call_flow.step_7_decline_or_timeout: If declined/30s timeout: ablyPublish('user:{callerId}', 'call_declined'|'call_missed'), room auto-deleted
call_flow.step_8_end_call: Any participant can call DELETE /api/calls/{roomName}, server deletes LiveKit room, both get call_ended event
call_flow.step_9_persist: Server writes call_history row (participants, duration, type, status)

infrastructure_changes.dockerfile_changes: No changes needed to Next.js Dockerfile. LiveKit runs as a separate container.
infrastructure_changes.network: Add livekit service to the existing docker-compose network so the Next.js app can reach it internally at http://livekit:7880

production_deployment.option_a: Self-host LiveKit on a separate VPS/container with a public IP. Requires open UDP port 7882 for WebRTC media.
production_deployment.option_b: LiveKit Cloud (cloud.livekit.io) – managed, no infra changes needed, usage-based pricing.
production_deployment.turn_server: LiveKit has built-in TURN relay for restrictive networks (truckers on cellular/firewalled WiFi). Enable in livekit.yaml: turn.enabled=true.

token_security: Tokens generated server-side only (LIVEKIT_API_SECRET never exposed to client)
Tokens are scoped: each token grants access to exactly one room
Token TTL: 5 minutes (enough to connect, not enough to be replayed)
Tokens include identity = userId so LiveKit room participants are identifiable
authorization: Only friends can call each other (enforced in POST /api/calls/initiate)
Callee token only issued after explicit accept action (GET /api/calls/token/:roomName)
Room auto-deleted after emptyTimeout=30s or via DELETE /api/calls/:roomName
Rate limit: 5 call initiations per minute per user
